full_judgment:
Mr. Latifur Rahman, C.J: This criminal petition for leave to appeal by the accused-petitioner is against the judgment and order passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1260 of 1999 by a Division Bench of the High Court Division affirming the order dated 15.2.99 rejecting the prayer of granting she petitioner Division in Jail in pending Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 7 of 1999. 

 2. The accused-petitioner filed an application under Section-561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the High Court Division and prayed for granting him Division- I /Class-1 in the Dhaka Central Jail. The accused-petitioner was awarded sentence of death in Bangabandhu Murder Case and death reference case No. 30 of 1998 is pending before the High Court Division for disposal. In such circum-stance, the accused-petitioner prayed for Division-1 in the jail custody while another case being Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 7 of 1999 is pending against him. So the primary question as to whether a person who is under a sentence of death and at the same time an under trial prisoner in another Sessions Case is entitled to Division-1 in the jail custody. 

 4. As per Section-30(2) of Prisoners Act, 1894 a prisoner shall be confined in a cell apart from all other prisoners and shall be placed by day and night under the charge of a guard. This is the normal procedure in case of a person who is suffering death sentence before confirmation of the High Court Division. In the present case, the petitioner is an under trial prisoner. In terms of Rule 617 of the Prisoner Act all convicted persons shall be divided into Three Division, namely I, II and III. Section-30(2) of the Prisoner Act, 1894 speaks of confinement in a cell from others. Hence Section-30 speaks of a special classification of a person who is under death sentence. Rule-617 is applicable to a convicted person and as such this rule is not applicable. In view of the fact that the present petitioner is also under a sentence of death and he is an under trial prisoner in another case the learned Judges observed as follows: 

 5. Before parting with the case, it may be said that Mahbubur Rahman made a complaint that the cell where the prisoner is kept at present is unfit for human habitation and the room has got no roof and the petitioner is living in an inhuman condition which is a violation of basic human rights.
